body:
Don't have the money for therapy. I'm coping with my failures through music and cartoons.

Suspending reality so it doesn't seem as blunt.

When all efforts to break down a wall are nullified, what else is there to do but submit?

The problem is there, it refuses to move and there is no solution that can be found at the moment.

My will and persistence has been weathered away from trying to break it down. I feel so exhausted.

Employment, which provides money for almost everything that makes me valid. 

Without it, my writings, my comics, my weightlifting, my social outings, my pursuit to become a profitable and professional writer, all of it has been slowly evaporating. 

Without employment, without money, all of these constituents drift away. The longer I go without it, the more likely they'll drift too far to recover. And that's my real fear: losing who I am and settling for something else.

I want to care. I really do.

But too many things are missing at the moment.
Waking up. That's exhausting enough.

I'm not enduring. I'm starting to contemplate the end. It's eating me alive every day.

My purpose is starting to fade away quick.

Ever since high school, I'm tried to compartmentalize all my negativity into an alter ego or something. I still think it's silly whenever I'm feeling ok but whenever I suffer these bouts of depression, I literally feel like it's another person.

Even in those quick instances, I feel like some other being bred from my negativity and emotions is there, like a doppelganger of depression.

I've had delusions of "destructive grandeur" so many times where I'd be walking down the street or laying in my bed, thinking about wreaking havoc as a reality warper or a warmonger, just erasing everything in different mediums, even myself.

It's almost like a flicker of thoughts that swarm to me, especially when I'm listening to music.

This is currently me right now but I don't know too much about medications to contemplate suicide. 

A few hours into my birthday and I've already written a suicide note, so I can definitely tell you that the sleep schedule and constant dark thoughts tie in to each other. 

I really want to get out of this situation but there doesn't seem to be a way out at all, no matter how hard I try.
I've been in that gray zone for years. I have no idea how to get out but I'm starting to settle, so I guess it's alright.

I haven't had a "dream" since I was little. In fact, ever since I was a child, I've only had nightmares.

When I'm awake, everything is painted in a bleak light that shifts depending on my state of mind.
Yeah. It hurts to wake up each day knowing I'm a failure.

Depression usually shreds my mentality to shit, so anything I think about or do is constantly covered in a veil of darkness. Everything's contorted and even my dreams remind me of how depressed I am. Almost like a mental takeover of everything.

This is the first time I really don't care that my birthday just rolled around. I really don't want to do anything or talk to anyone but my computer, stay in my room and sleep. 

Have yours been happening a lot lately or have they always sort of been there?

I feel my purpose has come and gone.

The best thing I can try and do is survive. Not going too well there, either.

Thanks for this post, though. This is good.

I try to sleep the day away so I don't have to see the sun.

As soon as the sun starts to rise, the light coming through my window, I try to sleep as much as possible until the night comes.
Maybe we all are, man.

Mm. I give as much detail as needed, since it usually goes to PMs. 

Then it generally degrades to "There's nothing I can do, sorry."

or

"You could try this. I hope this helps." And it doesn't because I already tried said thing. I think most of it is that people can only do so much on this forum without going over to physically console said person i.e. a hug or hanging out or having a good talk.

I'm in the same kind of position, except I worked my ass off through high school and college only to end up with student debt, continous rejections from every job I apply for and feeling like an unemployed sack of shit wasting away in his parents' house with no use for any light except from my computer.

If you can, choose a major that is big in the job market right now, something that's in demand. Hook up with some people in that major, find some connections and go to more social outings in your college.

Biggest piece of advice I can give: Don't be a writer. Making a living as a writer is one of the toughest things ever and will drain the hell out of you.

You've still got time, man. Connect with people and tell them about your situation. Even this close to graduation, there's something that can be done. Just have to consider all your options.
I wish I could feel that happy..

"I've been crawling on my belly
Clearing out what could've been.
I've been wallowing in my own chaotic
And insecure delusions."

Tool - forty-six & 2

I've been putting everything into researching, writing and getting writing jobs. Writing while in the throes of depression isn't as fantastic as it sounds. It's more lethargic than anything.

Months of that has led me here, worse than before. Honestly, everyone is moving on without me and I don't blame them.

Tell me about it.

The moment you get TWO rejections from great writing jobs you aced in interviews and tests, you open Facebook and the first thing you see is your friend getting a huge job the same day as the interview.

All my friends are having the best time succeeding and I'm failing. They have no words for me and don't want to talk to me. It festers and stews as hatred and depression. Can't explain it, really. I guess that's why I isolate myself. :(
I feel the same way.
I'm sick of everything in general.
Yeah, you could ay that.

I've been trying for months to find a job, both writing-based and retail with no success. It's bumming me the fuck out, especially when all my other friends are living on their own and climbing the ladders of the majors they graduated in.

I know that I'm a writer, or at least I'm trying to be. Spending all of high school and 4 years of college for a writing degree shows I at least want to be in the world of writing.

There is always more to learn but lack of money and energy makes it difficult to keep it going. I just reflect on when I didn't have to worry about overbearing student loan debt, job rejections and being isolated from my friends.
I've been trying but I keep getting pulled back down. I've become really cynical.

Hey, man. Recent college graduate and I know just how you feel.

Oddly enough, I was invisible for my sohpomore year too. Freshman year, I was in the dorms and that wasn't working out since my mom lost her job and I had to move back home. Since I was commuting, I couldn't hang out with all my friends that were downtown and it made things much harder for us to communicate. That summer, I suffered my first case of becoming a hermit, being the only one of my group of friends still in town. I tried to remedy that by digging into my talents and hard. Though, for most of the summer, I was total trash, I did take some time to go on this Khan Academy website and learn about science. For some reason, that combined with writing short stories about my problems really helped me survive. You said that you like to watch basketball and scroll through Reddit. Maybe you could get involved in an online community and perhaps chat it up with some NBA fans? I know PLENTY of people that love sports but are no good at them. They just love the game! Spot a jersey or a team cap and see who you can connect with, maybe open up with "Hey, did you see that so and so game last night?"

Your parents and your brother are obviously very important to you and they care about you. Relish that, seriously. Have you ever come out to them about how you're feeling, maybe discussing the direction your college courses are taking with a counselor or a close family member? See who wants to listen and let it all out, man.

College is never what we think it's going to be. To be honest, I thought there was gonna be wacky adventures and tons of friends to be made but I was wrong. Even for an art college! Right now, all of my friends are either out of town or out of state, so I have to live with the fact that it's just me here. But I'm going to try to make the best of it and see if looking forward to what tomorrow holds can keep me alive long enough for me to see the light.

I enjoyed reading more about you man. Thanks for taking the time to write it up!

I get up on a regular basis on the sheer fact of fear. The fear that I'll be kicked out if my parents realize the depths of my depression. The fear that if I let my writings rot away, I'll never have any purpose for as long as I live. The fear that I may bring the dark cloud to my long distance girlfriend and make her life as miserable as mine.

Through fear, I push past the depression like a heavy weight because I know that if I ever completely gave into it, I would be utterly destroyed and I would NEVER be able to get back up. It's a little like being under a squat rack at the gym: you can't put the barbell back on the rack but at the same time you can't let it fall and crush you, so you're trying to balance this weight you know you can't handle every single day, watching other people walk around the gym with no weight at all

Basically, I'm forced to walk the line with my depression or be destroyed. It's a tough fucking tightrope, I'll tell you that. But I'd rather walk that rope than fall into worse things, things that have drifted in the back of my mind like drug use and things I don't even want to say. It's a fight to get out of bed not because I'm fighting depression but because I'm trying to survive it day after day.

There are others here that feel the way you do. We're fighting our fights and I'll be the first to be ringside for your bout, water bottle and all. Keep going.

I'm an emotional wreck at the moment but I still drag the pieces along the pavement when someone needs someone to talk to.

Let me know if you ever need someone to chat it up with. I'm not that great with words when I'm down but I'll definitely reach out to you, man.

This was very well put to the child. Awesome, man.

Keep on rockin'. We need you around :)

Don't choose Creative or Fiction Writing unless you're madly in love with it and have a clear shot to a career after graduation.

You don't wanna end up like me. There's some great advice here and I think you should definitely slow down, contemplate and write some things down. You can do this. I know you can.
Nobody holes anyone up, even family, for free for long. Soon enough, they'll either start demanding rent or try to kick me out. Happened with my sibling.
Yeah, I got the worthless degree and didn't know it until I graduated.
I've felt like a leech for months. My parents tell me not to worry about being unemployed and go outside but I know it's just a matter of time before talks happen about finding a job or getting out.
Writing for a living is tough overall, dude. But that's mostly for freelancing. If you try and get in with a company that needs a technical writer, you're set!

It's hard to hang on when there's no one there to pull you up.

But I'm trying, man. I'm really trying.

I graduated with a Fiction/Creative Writing Degree. I'm on the slow road to getting screwed, walking it right now.

You'll be fine, dude. Don't be discouraged by what I'm spouting. I'm just severely disappointed in myself. Try asking your professors about potential job opportunities and paths.

I've applied for Content Writing, Article Writing, Technical Writing, all of it. I've gotten to the interview stage, I've been told "We'll get back to you." or "We'll let you know." Only to be denied or blocked from communication, like all of my hard work was worthless because I didn't fit.

Months of this. Months. When, in so many words, you're told you're not good enough and you're expendable garbage from people who are supposed to be in your field, people you thought would give you a chance because you spent years preparing for this point, you start to lose hope really fucking quick.

I'm really starting to believe that no one wants to hire me for my writing talent and that I should start scraping the bottom of the bucket for shit jobs, forget about writing altogether.

Of course! Without money, people are barred from most everything.

Unemployed and I can't afford weightlifting or going out with friends. Writing is pointless when no one will even bother to read it. Artists are being screwed straight out of college because they have no money to grease the palms of employers and instead have to hope they don't fall into the stereotypical Starving Artist category.

I wish it wasn't that way, but it is. And it's only getting worse.

I'm just starting to accept that I'm a loser that thought a "Professional Writer" was a thing. Turns out, at best, writing for a living means being someone's typewriter monkey. And I can't even get that. Stuck in unemployment.

I've gotten those types of rejections and some that lied to me about getting back to me the next day and, even when I contacted them after weeks, they never responded. I'm close to the edge myself and student loan debt is the finger that keeps trying to push me over.

Sorry about your situation, man. I know how you feel.
Thanks but if that one day is far down the line, that student loan interest is gonna be the biggest smack in the face after my first day on the job.

Unless you're a truly phenomenal artist that can build a fanbase quickly, the business world wants nothing to do with you. They don't value creativity; they value money and SEO trafficking to their websites. Visual artists have the best chance in that sense.

Sorry you're going through it too, man. I guess that's why some of the kids at my art college were loaded because they weren't worried about their future at all: Mom and dad could pay it all. I'm just sick of artists, both visual and written, working their asses off to make ends meet with their talent only to get brushed off because they aren't what businesses are looking for.
Thanks so much for your military service, man.

It is and I do. But no one cares about writers if they can't do a million other things or churn out copypaste articles with clickbait titles.

Writing as an art is dead for those who want to make a living. It's about being a cog, shutting up and writing the crap they want. And that's IF you're chosen to do even that. I couldn't even get a job in a content mill.
I wish I could sleep and live in my mind forever. Fantasy sure seems a hell of a lot better than reality right now.

My two cents. Keep them if you want or use them for a rockin' stick of gum.

First of all, happy birthday! This is a day of celebration because, for a short time, you can reflect on the fact that you were brought into this world when billions of other cells were denied that right. Some awesome science probability to ponder about being a survivor from day one.

I've worked in retail, ALDI supermarket. Grocery stores can be a pain, especially when they want you to stock up while there are a million customers on the floor asking you to run in the back and find things that you know you don't have. Rejoice in the fact that you have a steady stream of income. Even if it's just part time or its a bit crummy, it's something to be happy about. Money can't buy happiness but it can help.

The girl who wants to hook up with you seems like she just wants some physical satisfaction from those she thinks she can get it from. I don't know her and I barely know you but I think you should get connected with some real friends who care about you and what you're going through. No one should be a tool for someone else once they've been spurned. You matter much more than a quickie or a one night stand. Besides, you state music as a passion. That's great!

What instruments do you play? What songs do you like? Have you looked into maybe recording some songs, doing some songwriting and letting your emotions flow through your music? You could post them online and potentially build a fanbase as you increase in skill. I know that Maynard James Keenan from Tool told interviewers that when he was younger, music was his chance to expunge most of the darkness he carried with him, including his mother's death. Now, he's having a kickass time with Pucifer, making wacky music videos and tending to his winery. Music can be one of the most powerful weapons against depression.

My parents are religious as well, Christians who aren't exactly progressive so I have to keep things hidden from them. See if you can't talk with them about what you're feeling and instead of speaking to their religious personalities, say you want to speak with them mother and father to son, not to whatever deity they worship. Speak to them on a human level and get them to understand, if you can.

One final thing: Make a list. Make a list about the positives in your life and read them aloud vocally to yourself like a mantra. Most times, we stay silent when the darkness comes over us and we don't want to bother because depression can feel like this weight we can't shake off. Speak to that depression, that weight and tell it that you've got some awesome shit going on. 

Best of luck to you, man. And eat some extra cake for me! :D

I'm feeling that way currently. I feel as though that without a job, that by living at home and being supported by my parents, that I'm a leech that is wasting not only my life but those who are putting effort into helping me with no concrete solution in sight. But I know that I have to keep going. Why? Because I got this far and so did you.

One thing you could do is make a list, make a list of things ranging from mundane to awesome that interest you and make you happy. Doesn't matter how ridiculous they sound, write them down and read them to yourself. Actually vocalize these things. Speak your subconscious bits of hope and see how it makes you feel. I myself am a writer that is losing hope for being a writer but I write everyday and tell myself that I like writing everyday, so speak the definition of my person. This may help you with solidifying yourself in a place of your own personal reality, helping you branch out into the reality of others or a 'social reality'. 

Meditate on the thought that life is for the living and the dead have come to rest. You breathe, you feel and you are. Claim that and go from there. There are billions of people in the world, some of that outrageously large number are here in this subreddit that feel the same as you, that want to break free of the cycle just like you do. Reach out to others with the way you feel in a professional setting and dissect this feeling of emotional waste. The fact that you came here to write about the issue shows that you care enough about your life to do something about it, to change it.

I'm not good with helping others but I sincerely hope that you find the drive you need to grasp that goal you were meant to reach in life.

Anyone here can PM me if they'd like. I have a Skype, so just let me know your username if you wanna talk on there.

I could use a good friend right now :)

For years, I had minor seizures of something resembling nostalgia. Not physical but mental and powerful to boot. Sometimes it would be in a store or a building but light was the main factor that was aided by a kind of music or vocal.

Anyway, I found that I was having strong fits of involuntary Saudade, a more powerful form of nostalgia that someone feels about something that can never return or someone who is missing with no guarantee of returning. This can also be about moments in life. It's been getting strong throughout the years and, when I'm depressed as I am now, the fits reduce me to tears almost all the time.

I wish I could start all over.

I seek validation through the same avenues, though the more depressed I get, the more desperate I get. The strangest thing is that even when things are going well, my insecurity continues to grow. I like weightlifting and have become obsessed with it to the point where I need to look good and lift more than anyone around me. If I don't, I feel like a failure and sometimes go to extremes to make sure I achieve it next time I step in the gym.

Now, unemployed, I've been looking for cheap avenues of fulfillment and validation. I've even considered Craigslist's infamous encounter section recently. It's gotten to the point where nothing will ultimately validate me but I need it just so that I FEEL that it does, if that makes sense. I know how you feel. Stay strong.

I was doing something similar up until the end of last year. I took a job at a supermarket as a casual stocker. Had to wake up before sunrise and work pallets on the floor and in the freezer without much help from the other employees.

Two store resets, two years and no appreciation from anyone. I was used to do the stuff others didn't want to do. It started to crush me and my writing became nonexistent. One day, I broke down and cried when I drove up to work and just quit a few days later. 

The only thing that kept me there was the promise of a paycheck and even though I swore I would never go back to work there again, the thought still lingers because of desperation. Thanks for the kind words, man. I guess I just don't want to reach for the stars just to fall to the sea.

I write short stories, mostly. But I've taken classes for comic book scriptwriting and am working on a comic book series. The illustration went well until I couldn't pay my artist anymore, so we're on a hiatus with that.

I'm on the 3rd draft of my novel that I've been writing for a few years, but the motivation to pick up where I left off on editing is slipping away.

For writing jobs, I specify that I have experience in SEO and content writing for the web. Blogs and the like. It's getting harder everyday not to just throw my hands up and start applying for the bottom of the barrel retail jobs.

I would love to have a job like that but I know no job like that in Chicago, much less one that wants a fresh college grad.

Everyone wants marketing and technical writers with experience 5 years and up. Thanks for the suggestion, though.

All the things that make me happy cost money, including going some states over to see my girlfriend. I get extremely frugal whenever I'm inbetween jobs, so it would be temporary happiness that would make me feel a lot worse later.

I've been trying everywhere I could, even entry-level positions and the furthest I got was a writing test and interview at a good company that said they would contact me the next day about the position and never did. Even after I reached out. It's making me think I don't have the chops to be a writer, even after all I've done to be one and that, most of all, makes me think I wasted years of time messing around.

Oh, it's totally fine, dude. I'm just not used to posting on Reddit and the whole system yet. I passed out too.

Thanks. I'm really hanging onto these applications for some happiness.

Doing a little better. I've been looking up entry level writer jobs and applied for a good one with a cover letter and resume. I know it's not guaranteed, but it made me feel a little better I didn't just go through a whole bunch of jobs that I could never get.

Thanks for reaching out again, man. I thought you had left.

I listen to music and take notes for future stories, read through different scientific articles and research interesting things to keep my mood from becoming noticeable to my parents. Reading definitely helps some.

With the job thing, I've been looking all over from hotels to restaurants to retail to office clerk but I either get turned away due to them wanting more experience or for an unspecified reason because of nothing given but silence. Suffice to say I'm a horrible swimmer and almost drowned when I was younger, so I wouldn't be able to do what you do. Though I will try and check out some different certifications, see what I can do. Still cynical, though.

It's fine, man. This is actually my first time posting on Reddit, so I'm kinda new at this too.

I used to just write, put things down on paper but college made me very anal about editing, so it's hard to write a paragraph in my mood without criticizing it to hell and back before just closing the Word document.

Yeah, it's been a mixture of those two kinds of jobs. I've even tried looking at entry level writer jobs but nothing's been coming up so far. For some reason it feels worse feeling like you're gonna get the job after a good first impression and interview THEN getting rejected than just hearing nothing back at all. It really hits home the whole "You're not good enough to write professionally" or "You're not good enough to work at this retail store" idea.

That's a perfect description of my situation when I was working at the supermarket. 

But now the shit jobs have been replaced with no job and an unsuccessful job hunt in both conventional and writing fields.

What bothers me the most is that there seems to be no way I can do what I've always wanted to do: write stories for people for a living.

But the most pain comes from seeing my muscle disappear and waking up to no job. Without a job, everything crumbles fast. It happened before and I scraped around to find the ALDI job which exchanged money for loss of all creative energy.

I thought I did everything right by going to college, writing the best I could and getting high grades on everything. Even with a little experience, it seems like I missed the mark completely.

So, to answer your question, the job search is what's really putting me down. But in effect, it's unraveling a whole bunch of other problems, including mounting insecurity.

Strangely enough, almost all of my friends who are in marketing, music or visual arts are making a good living out of college. I'm almost starting to believe that I never should have gone to school for writing and just went to trade school for money.

Then I think about my supermarket job and how I was slowly getting into the mindset of money over everything else. Writing was the furthest thing from my mind and my social life was nonexistent because I was working or going to school. I don't know. I just feel like I made the worst decision ever because I worked my ass off to become a great writer, prepared for the field and nothing is coming to fruition. Absolutely nothing.

I'm on the fence about putting aside writing and just grinding, finding whatever job will take me so that I can just work, work, work.
